BLOCKER: New shipped logic (`review_block()`, `_latest_review()`, the `gate` subcommand, and the reworked `_ingest()` apply path) ships with zero test coverage. The operating standard — as applied to sibling item BI-PF-1429 in this same epic — treats missing tests for new shipped logic as a blocker. `scripts/dev/` Python is permitted by the language rule, but the test requirement is not waived.
MAJOR: Acceptance criterion "store on item + **gate sheet**" is only half-delivered: `gate` prints the latest evidence block to stdout. There is no persisted gate-sheet artifact, and no change to precheck / `config/ci-cd-gates.json` / merge-gate wiring — so findings are surfaced "IN the Gate 1/Gate 2 review" only if a human manually runs the script. The objective as written is not achieved by the diff.

The `ingest` subcommand never gained `--mode`, so `_ingest()` defaults to `"diff"` — a Gate 1.5 (design) review can never be recorded through the ingest path. `run` supports mode; `ingest` does not. Inconsistent ingestion channel undermines the two-gate symmetry the item exists to create.

`_post_context()` now posts `verification` as a single-element list, replacing whatever was there. Observable integrity impact: BI-PF-1429's live item had its prior verification — which recorded 2 BLOCKERs on untested network/secret-handling code — overwritten with "precheck PASS …". Prior blocker evidence is erased from the item of record; only the JSONL history retains it. The gate sheet must be append/merge or keyed, not wholesale replace.

`_ingest --apply` appends a full rendered review block to `evidence` on every run with no dedup by `(sha, mode)`. Re-runs across SHAs accumulate unbounded, contradictory blocks in one list; there is no notion of "current" Gate 1.5/2.5 finding, which is precisely what a gate sheet needs.

The `gate` subcommand returns exit code `0` even when the rendered review contains BLOCKER findings (only missing-evidence returns `1`). The printed recommendation says "BLOCKED" but the process exit status says success — a trap the moment this is wired into CI.

BI-PF-1429 was closed with delivery recorded and verification rewritten to "precheck PASS (architect-review gate satisfied by evidence)" while its own review still carried 2 BLOCKERs (no tests for new secret/network path; config-declared `api_key_env`/`api_key_file` contract silently ignored). The epic's own gate discipline is being bypassed to close its own items — closure should be re-verified against the recorded blockers.
MINOR: `_latest_review()` selects by filesystem `mtime`, which is not stable across fresh clones/CI checkouts (git does not preserve mtimes). "Latest review" can silently resolve to an arbitrary review; prefer an embedded timestamp or monotonic ordering in the evidence JSON.
Argparse now defines `--item` on both the parent parser and the `ing`/`gate` subparsers; behavior depends on subparser override semantics. Fragile and a maintenance trap.
`docs/BACKLOG-SUMMARY.md` was regenerated at 20:10, before BI-PF-1430 was created at 20:24 — the committed derived docs do not include the new item. Derived artifacts are being committed stale.

BI-PF-1430's body, acceptance criteria, in_scope, and approach are verbatim echoes of the title; the analysis itself flags "body/acceptance criteria thin" yet the item was auto-approved and marked ready. A change that touches gate integrity deserves a real AC (e.g., "findings visible in Gate 1/2 output AND persisted gate artifact AND enforced exit code").
NIT: The `"1.5" if mode == "design" else "2.5"` mapping is duplicated in `review_block`, `_ingest`, and the `gate` branch; a single helper would remove the drift risk when Gate 3 arrives.
Several data files land without trailing newlines (`closed.json`, item JSONs, `counters.json`) — inconsistent POSIX text-file convention; will produce noisy diffs in some tooling.
Output is `print`-only; no structured event/log line for "gate review surfaced" — harder to observe adoption of the new gate path.
SUMMARY: The change delivers a useful `review_block` renderer and a `gate` inspection subcommand, but the stated objective — findings surfaced IN the Gate 1/2 review with a persisted gate sheet — is not wired into any gate flow, and the ingest path cannot record design-mode reviews at all.

Top risks: (1) untested shipped logic per the project's own standard; (2) `verification`/`evidence` clobber-and-append semantics that erase and then bloat the item of record — observable now in BI-PF-1429, where recorded BLOCKERs were overwritten and the item closed; (3) exit-code semantics that would let a BLOCKED gate pass once automated.

Recommend: add tests, key findings by `(sha, mode)` with an explicit "current" pointer, make context updates merge rather than replace, thread `--mode` through ingest, return non-zero on blockers, and actually wire `gate` into the Gate 1/2 review path before claiming the AC.
